memory_update.text: SABR is the primary US-listed reference anchor for travel distribution middleware because its GDS directly monetizes travel bookings through transaction fees.
AGYS should remain in the underfollowed lane as a hotel/resort property operating-system candidate with PMS, POS, payments, inventory, and guest-experience modules.
PRO belongs in the underfollowed airline-offer infrastructure lane; the key question is whether airline retailing and AI/NDC changes expand or bypass its role.
WEX is a payments-routing candidate for B2B travel settlement and virtual cards, but later layers must separate travel contribution from fleet and non-travel corporate payments.

US-listed pure-play hotel channel managers and PMS vendors are scarce; many relevant names such as SiteMinder, Mews, Duetto, Travelport, and ATPCO are non-US-listed or private, so public-market mapping may require ADR/foreign-listing and private-company customer checks in later passes.
SABR remains the US-listed reference rail for travel distribution/GDS exposure, but must be treated as a restructuring/debt-sensitive reference rather than a clean underfollowed discovery name.

AGYS is a promising underfollowed PMS/POS/property-connectivity candidate for hotel infrastructure exposure; verify whether PMS deployments and integrations, not only POS/casino software, are driving growth.
FOUR is a travel-payments discovery candidate because hospitality integrations and the Global Blue acquisition create exposure to cross-border travel spend, DCC, and tax-free shopping infrastructure.
RSKD is a small-cap fraud/chargeback layer candidate with travel-specific evidence through airline/OTA/hotel fraud analysis and Outpayce partnership; materiality to revenue remains unverified.

Several relevant pure-play travel technology assets are not currently clean US-listed candidates: SiteMinder is ASX-listed, Amadeus is primarily Madrid-listed/OTC ADR, and PROS has been taken private.
Add SABR as the US-listed reference rail for travel distribution middleware, but mark leverage/restructuring and NDC disintermediation as key later-layer risks.
Add WEX to the underfollowed lane as a virtual-card and B2B supplier-payment infrastructure candidate for OTAs and travel intermediaries.
Add RSKD to the underfollowed lane as a small-cap travel fraud/chargeback candidate due to the 2026 Outpayce/Amadeus airline-payments integration.
Add AGYS as an underfollowed property-connectivity and hotel-operations software candidate; verify whether PMS/POS integrations create durable distribution/payment/loyalty chokepoint exposure.

Several highly relevant hotel-connectivity names appear non-US-listed or private, including SiteMinder, RateGain/DHISCO, Shiji, Cloudbeds, Mews, Travelport, and Outpayce/Amadeus. Later passes should decide whether non-US listings are allowed or retained only as context anchors.

SABR is the most direct US-listed small-cap mapping for travel distribution middleware/GDS exposure, but the thesis must be stress-tested against NDC bypass risk, leverage, and transaction-volume cyclicality.

AGYS maps to the property-connectivity/PMS layer and may be underfollowed because it is labeled hospitality software rather than travel infrastructure; verify whether large PMS deployments create durable switching costs.
FLYW is a second-order travel-payments candidate, but travel is only one vertical; future layers need vertical revenue/payment-volume evidence before upgrading confidence.
RSKD is a speculative underfollowed fraud/chargeback layer for travel and ticketing; key evidence gap is durable vertical mix and unit economics through fraud-cycle volatility.

Important non-US or non-public comparables for the node include Amadeus, Travelport, SiteMinder, Oracle Hospitality, and private hotel-tech vendors; use them as competitive context but keep this funnel US-listed.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around travel distribution and transaction infrastructure. The reference anchor is Sabre because it owns one of the core GDS rails and explicitly monetizes bookings through GDS transaction fees. The underfollowed lane contains hospitality property/POS/payments software, airline offer/pricing infrastructure, and B2B travel virtual-card payment rails. No investment recommendation is made; these are research candidates for later evidence, pricing, and falsification layers. Layer 1B expands the scarce-supplier universe around travel distribution and transaction infrastructure rather than consumer-facing OTAs, airlines, or hotels. The strongest US-listed discovery candidates found in this pass are middleware/payment/fraud vendors whose economics are tied to fragmented supplier connectivity, hotel operating systems, card-not-present travel payments, cross-border authorization, and chargeback control. SABR is included as the obvious GDS/reference rail; AGYS, FOUR, and RSKD are the more underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery lane. Global Blue was relevant as a travel/cross-border payments asset but is now part of Shift4, so exposure is mapped through FOUR rather than as a standalone candidate. Expanded the US-listed universe around the travel distribution/payments/fraud infrastructure node with a two-lane funnel.
